Adding a photo of your yard over a plan you’d already drawn, then setting its scale, no longer asks whether to move the plan with the photo: nothing was drawn over it.
Plant names in a saved picture or a printout are drawn over the plants beside them, never half under a taller one.
On a small phone, the notice about plants placed too close keeps all its buttons on screen, and while you’re placing it stays until you do something else.
Counting plants you bought in the Plant list with + no longer misses the second press: the list doesn’t jump after the first.
Clear filters in the plant list leaves who’s in your yard as it is; each one’s own chip turns it off. The list opens at its usual height each time.
On a small phone with the keyboard up, the plant search folds For and Filters away so the results show.
